newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO CRASHES OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO CRASHES OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: World number three Arantxa Sanchez Vicario crashed out of the Australian Open in the third round on Saturday in her worst Grand Slam performance for five years.
The Spanish second seed was beaten by Belgian Dominique van Roost 1-6 6-4 8-6 on Centre Court in the biggest upset of the women's draw to date.
Sanchez Vicario, a losing finalist in five of the last eight grand slam events, faded badly after leading 5-2 in the decisive third set to succumb in two hours and 14 minutes.
"She had nothing to lose and everything was on her side. She played very well, but I let go of the match," Sanchez Vicario told reporters.
"I am very disappointed because I had my chances and if you let them go, you can lose matches, which is what happened."
Van Roost, ranked 43rd in the world, needed several minutes of medical treatment on a sore muscle in her right arm before serving out the match.

"The treatment helped me to relax a little before the last game," said Van Roost, a natural baseliner who attributed her victory to a rigorous training routine over recent months to improve her strength and stamina.
"I try to be aggressive with my shots and if I hadn't gone to the net and put her under pressure I don't think I would have won," the slender Van Roost said.
Her reward for beating the gritty Spaniard is a fourth round encounter with American 15th seed Chanda Rubin.
"I set myself a goal of beating a top 10 player this year and now I have achieved that. I am very happy," Van Roost said.

A despondent Sanchez Vicario said the mental strength that lifted her to the world number one ranking two years ago would stand her in good stead after so many recent disappointments. She lost to American Amy Frazier at a warm-up tournament in Sydney 10 days ago.

"I cannot let it bother me that I missed out in so many finals. I know my turn will come. The past is the past and I have just to keep going," said Sanchez Vicario, a finalist at Melbourne Park in 1994 and 1995 and three-time Grand Slam winner at the French and U.S. Opens.

Although it was the biggest win of Van Roost's career, perhaps the player who gains most from Sanchez Vicario's surprise exit is Swiss prodigy Martina Hingis, the fourth seed, who now has a seemingly clear run to the final following the earlier exit of sixth seed Iva Majoli of Croatia.
Hingis was to play to play unseeded Austrian Barbara Schett in another third round tie on Saturday evening.
Van Roost, who has never advanced beyond the fourth round at a Grand Slam, came to Melbourne in fine form after winning a warm-up event in Hobart last week.
Rubin booked her passage with a 6-1 6-3 win over qualifier Sandra Kleinova of the Czech Republic.
In other matches on Saturday, men's fifth seed Thomas Muster and eighth seed Wayne Ferreira of South Africa cruised through to the last 16.
Spanish 10th seed Albert Costa followed compatriots Felix Mantilla, seeded 14th, and unseeded Carlos Moya into the fourth round by beating Australian Scott Draper in straight sets.

But in a mixed day for Spain, 16th seed Alberto Berasategui was forced to retire in the fourth set of his match against Slovakia's Dominik Hrbaty because of leg cramps. Hrbaty was leading 6-3 7-6 6-7 2-0.
In the women's draw, eighth-seeded Romanian Irina Spirlea and ninth seed Karina Habsudova of Slovakia advanced with straight-sets victories.
